newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine lawmakers agree on mortgage bank sale.
newsitem.headline: Argentine lawmakers agree on mortgage bank sale.

text.p: The Argentine government and congressmen from the ruling Peronist Party struck a deal Tuesday to privatize state mortage lender Banco Hipotecario over three years.
The privatization will be carried out "in stages over the next three years," Jorge Rodriguez, President Carlos Menem's Cabinet Chief, told reporters. Final approval by Congress is expected in March.
The sale is set to take place over three years to prevent a monopoly from developing in the mortgage market, Rodriguez said after a meeting with lawmakers.

The agreement with congressmen includes a proposal to generate "resources to grant credits for the construction of 50,000 houses," said Rodriguez. It is hoped this construction drive will create some 200,000 new jobs.
Those resources would be established in order to finance up to 95 percent of the cost of mortgage loans.
Last week, Jorge Matzkin, the Peronist Party whip in the lower house of Congress, suggested Banco Hipotecario would issue a $500 million bond to raise the funds.
The local media has reported that the government plans to retain a "golden share" or right to veto after privatization. The government expects to raise $3.0 billion from the sale.
